audience.text: C++ developers building desktop, server, or embedded applications that require PDF document processing without external runtime dependencies.

capabilities.text: Open existing PDFs, including password-protected ones, and save changes with optional incremental updates preserving original bytes.
capabilities.title: Open and edit PDF documents

capabilities.text: Extract full text using TextAbsorber or positioned fragments using TextFragmentAbsorber, and read/write document metadata via DocumentInfo and Metadata.
capabilities.title: Extract text and metadata

capabilities.text: Render pages to PNG, JPEG, BMP, or TIFF with configurable resolution and palette options, using PngDevice, JpegDevice, BmpDevice, and TiffDevice.
capabilities.title: Render pages to images

capabilities.text: Apply encryption using RC4-40, RC4-128, AES-128, or AES-256 with granular Permissions flags, and sign with detached PKCS#7 using Facades::PdfFileSignature.
capabilities.title: Encrypt and sign documents

capabilities.text: Build documents with positioned text, tables, vector graphics, watermarks, annotations, AcroForm fields, outlines, and embedded files.
capabilities.title: Create PDFs from scratch

capabilities.text: Use Standard-14 fonts via system fonts or bundled Liberation substitutes, with fallback for 12 of 14 fonts.
capabilities.title: Support for standard fonts

capabilities.text: Use Facades classes like PdfConverter, PdfExtractor, PdfFileSignature, PdfFileEditor, and PdfFileStamp for procedural workflows.
capabilities.title: Facades API for legacy workflows

limitations.text: Standard-14 font fallback covers only 12 of 14 fonts; Symbol and ZapfDingbats have no bundled fallback.
XmpValue type-checking helpers (IsDateTime, IsField, etc.) are stubs that always return false.
Setting metadata on a from-scratch document and saving throws because there is no /Info object to patch.
Permissions set via encryption are enforced by the consuming PDF viewer, not by the library itself.

problems_solved.text: Enables PDF document reading, text extraction, and rendering to images without linking to commercial or third-party PDF libraries.
Supports encryption, decryption, and digital signing of PDFs using standard algorithms and formats.
Provides a modern C++20 API for building PDFs from scratch including text, tables, graphics, forms, and annotations.

product_summary.text: Aspose.PDF FOSS for C++ is a free, open-source C++20 library for creating, editing, and processing PDF documents with no runtime dependencies.

uncertainties: The exact set of supported AcroForm field types beyond those explicitly listed in examples is unclear.
Whether all Facades classes support all operations documented in the README is not fully verifiable from facts.
The behavior of TiffDevice for multi-page output beyond the example is not confirmed.
The scope of 'byte-verbatim round-trips' for saved documents is not detailed beyond metadata updates.
The exact behavior of FontRepository::FindFont when system fonts are unavailable is not specified.
Whether the library supports PDF/A or PDF/UA conformance is not stated.
The exact set of supported image formats for embedding via AddImage is not confirmed.
The runtime behavior of Document::Decrypt when the password is incorrect is not specified.

workflows.name: Open and inspect PDF
workflows.text: Open a PDF file, count pages, read metadata, and extract text using Document, PageCollection, DocumentInfo, and TextAbsorber.

workflows.name: Render pages to images
workflows.text: Render individual or multiple pages to PNG, JPEG, BMP, or TIFF using PngDevice, JpegDevice, BmpDevice, or TiffDevice.

workflows.name: Encrypt or sign a document
workflows.text: Apply encryption with user/owner passwords and granular permissions, or sign with a detached PKCS#7 signature.

workflows.name: Build a document from scratch
workflows.text: Create a new Document, add pages, insert text, tables, vector shapes, watermarks, annotations, and form fields.
